title: Jeff Bezos Was ‘Heavily Involved’ in Casting Robert Pattinson as James Bond and Admits Initial Fears ‘Because He’s Already So Famous’

body:
Amazon founder and chairman Jeff Bezos revealed during a recent appearance at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event that he was “heavily involved” in Amazon MGM casting Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond. 

	Bezos said that because Bond is traditionally a star-making role, they were at first “slightly biased” against casting Pattinson because he’s already “so famous.” However, after narrowing down the candidates to five and conducting screen tests, he was the “obvious” choice. 
	

	“We ran a really tight process and made the final decision on Friday,” Bezos said. “There was a big group initially, and we down-selected to five finalists. We did real, old-fashioned screen tests of those five finalists. It was interesting. Full costumes and real sets and other actors with them. We did three different scenes with each of the five finalists, and then we got together on Friday to spend a couple of hours looking at all the tests and reviewing all that.”

	He continued, “By the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing. But there was something special about Rob and his performance. It was immediately undebated. Denis [Villeneuve], the director … we all gravitated toward Rob. Initially, we were slightly biased against him just because he’s already so famous, like maybe we should have somebody more unknown, but in the screen tests, it was so obvious he is James Bond.”

	Amazon MGM announced Pattinson as the next James Bond on Monday, ending weeks of rabid media speculation. “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” the “Batman” and “Primetime” star said in a statement after the news broke. “I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”
	

	While Bezos never mentioned them by name, industry analysts seemingly had a handle on the Bond finalists heading into the last weekend of casting. The shortlist of top choices included Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor, Jack Lowden and Nicholas Hoult. Other names rumored to be in the running at one include Jacob Elordi, Tom Francis, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Harris Dickinson and even Harry Styles.

	Amazon finalized its deal for MGM, the studio behind James Bond, in 2022. However, it didn’t have creative control of the franchise until it bought out longtime Bond producers Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli for $20 million. Denis Villeneuve and Pattinson’s film will be the first released after the deal.

	The actress, who reprises her beloved role as Katniss in the prequel film, walked the carpet in a floor-length black silk coat from Jonathan Anderson’s Dior Pre-Fall 2026 collection. The robe-like design featured an oversized white fur collar, colorful floral embroidery cascading down one side and a dramatic front slit, which Lawrence paired with black satin mules by Gianvito Rossi and vintage diamond-and-onyx earrings from Fred Leighton.


	The boudoir-inspired silhouette, which combines silky fabrics, sweeping hemlines and oversized fur collars, has become a favorite among designers and celebrities alike. London-based designer Conner Ives helped popularize the look with his demi-couture silk robes, first introduced on his Fall 2025 runway and subsequently worn by Zoë Kravitz, Sienna Miller, Hailey Bieber and Kendall Jenner. title: CMA Awards Predictions: Expect Ella Langley to Get Everything but Male Vocalist, and Maybe Even That’s Not Safe
description:
Nov 17, 2026 2:41pm PT

body:
Nov 17, 2026 2:41pm PT	
	

	
		CMA Awards Predictions: Expect Ella Langley to Get Everything but Male Vocalist, and Maybe Even That’s Not Safe
	

	Variety is picking the winners for the 2026 CMAs, with plenty of easy-to-place bets on 9x-nominated Ella Langley. But it ain't over till the EOTY sings.
	
			


			
			
	

									WireImage
	

		
	
				


	The suspense is unbearable: Will the 2026 CMA Awards see Ella Langley enjoying a total sweep, or just a near-sweep?

	That is a real question, not a rhetorical one. But before we start trying to anticipate the math, let’s remember that, although Langley had a leading nine nominations, the most she can win is seven, because she is competing against herself in two categories, single of the year and song of the year, where “Choosin’ Texas” is up against “Be Her.” Normally that would leave room for vote-splitting, but rest assured, Langley and her two-stepping two-timers have the means to overcome that little problem. So with best single and best song utterly in the bag, that leaves five more open to see if she can run the board with the Country Music Association’s voters.

	Entertainer of the Year, especially? There is some real suspense there. In some matters, it does take a crystal ball to see.

	Here are our predictions for the winners of the 60th annual awards, which air live from Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena from 8-11 on the east coast and delayed for prime on the west coast, also at 8. 

	ENTERTAINER OF THE YEAR

	Luke CombsCody JohnsonElla LangleyChris StapletonLainey Wilson

	Will win: Ella LangleyCould win: Cody Johnson

	This top honor used to be regarded as something closer to an ongoing lifetime achievement award for a currently hot superstar than a recognition of pure, recent artistic achievement that could go to someone in the earlier stages of a long ascent. But it felt like that was starting to change when Lainey Wilson got it in 2023 without having developed any severe road wrinkles. (She also got it again in 2025.) All of which is to say that there is a question that could be asked with Lainey and this honor: “Too soon?” And the likely answer to that is: “Nope, but thanks for asking.”

	Still, there is a lane open here for anyone to bust through if voters should decide that an armful of “lesser” awards are good enough for Langley this year. No one would greatly begrudge the well-love Wilson getting it for the third time in four years. Combs is probably the longest shot, being a two-time winner, like Langley. Neither Stapleton nor Johnson have gotten it even once. Stapleton has the “seriously, overdue” factor in his favor, having been nominated 11 times without ever taking it home. But if the enthusiasm for keeping it fresh continues but it’s just not Langley’s time for it, Johnson feels most like a presumptive second-place — and possibly first-place — finisher.

	Still, the vast mainstream/crossover audiences watching the show at home will scratch their chins if it’s anyone but Langley, who has two of the biggest songs of the year in any genre in “Choosin’ Texas” and “Be Her” and has undoubtedly become country’s biggest ambassador to the world for this particular time frame. Choosin’ anyone else would just seem strangely insular.



	SINGLE OF THE YEAR

	“Be Her” – Ella Langley“Choosin’ Texas” – Ella Langley“I Knew It, I Knew You” – Taylor Swift“Somewhere Over Laredo” – Lainey Wilson“The Fall” – Cody Johnson

	Will win: “Choosin’ Texas”Could win: Get real. Are you insane?

	If “Choosin’ Texas” didn’t exist, we might be supposed that Langley would still be a front-runner for the award, but for “Be Her.” According to data provided to Variety by Luminate, “Be Her” is the all-around third most-consumed song of 2026 among all genres, not just country. But “Choosin’ Texas” is one of the biggest hits (use your Kanye voice here) of all time, as it currently enjoys a record-extending 28th week at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. Moreover, there is no resentment in the country community against its success, and certainly none against Langley for crossing over when the song America can’t stop falling for is as country as country can be. Seeing a shoo-in get shooed in never felt any better.

	But, needless to say, boy, are the CMAs producers glad Taylor Swift is nominated here. Surely she knows she is not going to beat Langley here, and she is happy to show up and perform anyway… as a thank-you to the ones who brought her to the dance, and also, maybe, a campaign stop on the way to a place where more is at stake.

	ALBUM OF THE YEAR

	Ain’t In It For My Health – Zach TopDandelion – Ella LangleyMiddle of Nowhere – Kacey MusgravesParker McCollum – Parker McCollumThe Way I Am – Luke Combs

	Will win: “Dandelion”Could win: “Parker McCollum”

	It’s hard to imagine the scenario where an album as across-the-board as good as “Dandelion” doesn’t follow “Choosin’ Texas” into the winners’ circle. But there’s a case voters can reasonably make for casting their ballots for anything else in the category. Musgraves’ “Middle of Nowhere” was the most critically acclaimed country album of the year overall, and marked a definitive return to country after some musically farther-afield records from the star. It would be wonderful to see Kacey finally get it, many of us can agree. But only occasionally do voters go for an album that didn’t have a huge impact at mainstream country radio, as evidence by the fact that Musgraves’ often left-of-center approach has landed her four prior nominations in this category but only one win (for “Golden Hour”). 

	Still, this is the category where voters are most apt to sometimes break ranks with bestselling stuff and pick something cool to make a statement. (Think Lee Ann Womack’s “There’s More Where That Came From” in 2005.) So that could mean it’s back to being Musgraves’ time… or it could mean they’d have a hankering for Parker McCollum’s critically acclaimed, self-titled album, in which he was seen as going for artistry more than hits. The fact that the ACM Awards gave McCollum this award back in the spring definitely should be taken into account in reading the tea leaves. But realistically, it just seems like we’ll never know which of those albums came in second… because how can Langley lose?



	SONG OF THE YEARAward goes to Songwriter(s)

	“Be Her”Songwriters: Smith Ahnquist, Michael Hardy, Ella Langley, Jordan Schmidt“Beautiful Things”Songwriters: Jessi Alexander, Jessie Jo Dillon, Connie Harrington, Megan Moroney“Choosin’ Texas”Songwriters: Luke Dick, Ella Langley, Miranda Lambert, Joybeth Taylor“Dry Spell”Songwriters: Luke Laird, Shane McAnally, Kacey Musgraves, Josh Osborne“Gary”Songwriter: Stephen Wilson Jr.

	Will win: “Choosin ’Texas”Could win: Get real, again.

	It’s hard to remember when the CMA Awards had a greater crop of songs up for this honor than this year. Can they make it a five-way tie and everyone gets a prize? No, they cannot. So as much applause as we might want to hold in reserve for Musgraves, Megan Moroney or Stephen Wilson Jr., this particular prize has had Langley’s name on it since before the creation of the world. Not to get biblical.

	FEMALE VOCALIST OF THE YEAR

	Miranda LambertElla LangleyMegan MoroneyKacey MusgravesLainey Wilson

	Will win: Ella LangleyCould win: No other option. The need to get real persists.

	If you were making a list of the five most outstanding artists in country music in the 2020s, you could pick these five without any shame or need to move on… even if we might eventually worry we’d overlooked a guy or two. But honestly, what a field. Anyway it’s Langley’s to lose.

	MALE VOCALIST OF THE YEAR

	Luke CombsCody JohnsonChris StapletonZach TopStephen Wilson Jr.

	Will win: Ella Langley. No, just kidding. Cody JohnsonCould win: Stephen Wilson Jr.

	We should probably look at which three artists from this field are also nominated for entertainer of the year, and narrow it down from there. Of those three, Johnson has the freshest momentum, even though Combs and Stapleton are not a bit less popular than they ever were. You could never go wrong with virtually anyone in the world by naming Stapleton the male vocalist of this or any year, but he might have simply won it too many times. It would be a news-making upset if Wilson should get in — the odds are really stacked against him amid these proven heavyweights, but there is so much appreciation for him that a big cheer would go up if he crashed through that ceiling. 




	VOCAL GROUP OF THE YEAR

	Lady ALittle Big TownMidlandOld DominionThe Red Clay Strays

	Will win: The Red Clay StraysCould win: Old Dominion

	The vocal group and vocal duo categories tend to have the least fresh blood and the most predictable year-by-year streaks The Red Clay Strays were a surprise winner last year — no one was more surprised than them — so it’ll be interesting to see if that was a one-off or the start of yet another CMA streak. I’m betting the latter, not least of all because they’re basically a rock group, and country people love having a real rock group — a good one — to bring some rootsy energy and fierceness into the genre. 

	VOCAL DUO OF THE YEAR

	Brooks & DunnBrothers OsborneDan + ShayMuscadine BloodlineThelma & James

	Will win: Brooks & DunnCould win: Brothers Osborne

	Just as much as CMA voters have liked having some new blood to vote for, in the form of the Red Clay Strays, they have enjoyed going back to Brooks & Dunn to celebrate old-home week. They’ve won this 16 times, and finally returned to the winners’ circle last year after previously last getting it in 2018. Their comeback as awardees here still feels fresh, in that sense, even if it’s a feat as old as time immemorial for them. 


	MUSICAL EVENT OF THE YEAR

	“A Song To Sing” – Miranda Lambert (with Chris Stapleton)“Horses and Divorces” – Kacey Musgraves (feat. Miranda Lambert)“I Can’t Love You Anymore” – Ella Langley & Morgan Wallen“If I Don’t Leave I’m Gonna Stay” – Carly Pearce & Riley Green“McArthur” – HARDY, Eric Church, Morgan Wallen & Tim McGraw

	Will win: “I Can’t Love You Anymore”Could win: “Horses and Divorces”

	This one is actually a tough category to call. The Langley/Wallen duet will probably get swept in on the wave that is pushing Ella toward so many other noms, and there continues to be support for Wallen in many pockets of the industry, even though you wouldn’t know it from the lack of nominations he’s gotten since winning entertainer of the year two years ago. But although their song served its purpose as something for them to sing together on his tour, is it really up there with Langley’s best songs or more of an agreeable time-passer? If it should fail to ride through on her long coattails, it’s tough to know where things go from there. I’m partial to the sensual Pearce/Green duet, and wish Pearce was up for a lot more for her excellent album. 

	But damn it, “Horses and Divorces” actually was an event, if you’re going to take the title of the trophy seriously. After a long, low-simmering feud no one denied, Musgraves had the brilliant idea to call Lambert up for a peace-pipe session, in the guise of a songwriting section about their feud… to great comedic-yet-real effect Talk about working it out on the remix. As Clint Eastwood once said, though, deserve’s got nothin’ to do with it. So expect Langley to need to build an extra shelf.



	MUSIC VIDEO OF THE YEAR

	“Choosin’ Texas” – Ella Langley“Dry Spell” – Kacey Musgraves“Gary” – Stephen Wilson Jr.“The Fall” – Cody Johnson“White Horse” – Chris Stapleton

	Will win: “Choosin’ Texas”Could win: “Dry Spell” or “Gary”

	“Choosin’ Texas” isn’t really the most interesting video of all of these, but it gets the job done, and that should be enough to have it two-step its way into the winners’ circle. Still, maybe this is the place for voters to exercise a fondness for Musgraves, via her amusing video about sexual frustration in the supermarket. As Freud said, sometimes a cucumber is not just a cucumber.

	NEW ARTIST OF THE YEAR

	Avery AnnaCarter FaithEmily Ann RobertsTucker WetmoreStephen Wilson Jr.

	Will win: Tucker WetmoreCould win: Stephen Wilson Jr.

	Wetmore is the only one here with No. 1 hits, which ought to be enough to push him across the line as voters face the inevitable question of how they think their choice will hold up 10 or 15 years from now. He’d be a worthy winner, but so would any of the others, most of all the critically beloved Faith and Wilson. Faith just picked up a key Grammy nomination… which of course means little in this context, but just saying… she’s interesting and she’s a keeper. So is Wilson, who has a much larger profile at present, including a lot of left-over love from how he killed it on last year’s telecast, twice. Wetmore is the horse to bet on, but this might be closer to a photo finish than most would suspect.



	
		More from Variety

schema.headline: CMA Awards Predictions: Expect Ella Langley to Get Everything but Male Vocalist, and Maybe Even That’s Not Safe

title: Marvel Started Planning for Robert Downey Jr.’s Doctor Doom Before Jonathan Majors Was Fired and ‘Avengers: The Kang Dynasty’ Fell Apart, Says Kevin Feige
description: Before “Avengers: Doomsday,” there was “Avengers: The Kang Dynasty.” Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige announced the latter title at Comic-Con in Jul
body:
Before “Avengers: Doomsday,” there was “Avengers: The Kang Dynasty.” Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige announced the latter title at Comic-Con in July 2022, with Jonathan Majors’ Kang the Conqueror poised to become the Marvel Cinematic Universe’s next Thanos-sized villain starting with 2023’s “Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania.”

	Those plans, however, were upended a few weeks after “Quantumania” opened in theaters and earned some of Marvel’s worst reviews and box office. Majors was arrested in March 2023 after he assaulted his then-girlfriend in the backseat of a private vehicle. The actor was officially convicted in December 2023, with a six-person jury finding him guilty of two misdemeanor counts of harassment and assault. Marvel did not hesitate to cut ties with him, firing Majors immediately after his conviction was announced. The actor was then sentenced in April 2024 to one year of domestic violence counseling.
	

	With Majors’ firing, the Marvel Cinematic Universe would be overhauled, with “Avengers: The Kang Dynasty” being replaced by “Avengers: Doomsday.” The plan now moved to bringing back Robert Downey Jr. to the MCU, only this time not as Iron Man (who died in 2019’s “Avengers: Doomsday) but as the villainous Doctor Doom. However, Marvel Studios boss revealed in the latest issue of Empire magazine (via The Playlist) that Doom was in the conversation to be added to the MCU well before “The Kang Dynasty” fell apart amid Majors’ legal troubles.

	“It probably would still have been called ‘The Kang Dynasty,’ but it would have been a set-up for Doom, midway through that movie,” Feige said, revealing the plan for “The Kang Dynasty” was actually for it to be a bait-and-switch movie in which Doom was revealed as the real Thanos-sized villain of the MCU’s multiverse saga.
	

	According to Feige, Marvel first got in touch with Robert Downey Jr’s agent (telling him: “We have an idea, it’s time”) around the same time as the “Quantumania” premiere in February 2023, weeks before Majors’ arrest in New York City. 

	“It was very delicate,” Feige added about the Majors situation. “We didn’t want to rush into any rash decisions in terms of employment. People think there was a cause-and-effect with Jonathan’s issues, and that certainly accelerated some things. But the Doom of it all was well underway before that… ‘Quantumania’ was not received the way we would have liked. There are many elements of that that we’re proud of, the Kang performance being one of them. But we were changing [‘The Kang Dynasty’] even at that point.”

	“Avengers: Doomsday” opens in theaters Dec. 18.

body:
The kids competition series “Shrunk” has been greenlit at Amazon Kids+, CBC, and ITV, Variety has learned exclusively. 

	The first season will consist of six 30-minute episodes. The format hails from Insight Productions, Dark Slope, and Irad Eyal (“Floor Is Lava”). Pre-production is currently underway, with shooting set to begin in January 2027 at Dark Slope’s 75,000 sq. ft. production facility in Toronto. Insight’s Mark Lysakowski serves as showrunner.
	

	In the show, kids are dropped into a giant world that “shrinks” them to two inches tall. They must work through challenges like catapulting meatballs through the air and pushing a massive skee ball down the lane of a carnival midway, utilizing teamwork and strategy skills. 

	“Every kid wonders what it would be like to be two inches tall, where a kitchen counter becomes a mountain and a puddle becomes a lake — ‘Shrunk’ finally shows them,” said Aaron Berman, Head of Originals for Kids+. “It’s imaginative, it’s messy, and it’s unlike anything else in kids’ competition TV. We’re thrilled to have it join our collection of unscripted competition shows on Kids+.”

	“Shrunk” is slated to premiere on Amazon Kids+, CBC, and ITV in 2027. Amazon Kids+ holds rights for the U.S., Mexico, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, and Spain, with shared rights in Canada (CBC) and the UK (ITV).

	“’Shrunk’ will entertain and delight young audiences, and inspire them to imagine their own larger-than-life adventures,” said Marie McCann, Senior Director, Children’s Content, CBC Kids. “We’re excited to share the series with kids and families across Canada.”
	

	Shrunk is created by Atoosa Mohajer and Dan Fill for Dark Slope; Tanya Low and Lysakowski for Insight Productions; and Eyal. Executive producers are Raja Khanna, Executive Chair and Co-Founder, Dark Slope, and John Brunton CEO & Chair, Insight Productions. Alex Kitz is Chief Business Officer & Legal Counsel for Insight. For CBC, Sally Catto is General Manager, Entertainment; Marie McCann is Senior Director, Children’s Content, CBC Kids; and Swin Chang is Executive in Charge of Development and Production, CBC Kids.

	“This promises to be an exciting, hilarious and messy affair with huge ketchup showers and oversized mud puddles, combined with the fantasy fulfillment of being teeny tiny,” said Atoosa Mohajer, Head of Development at Dark Slope.

	“We’re delighted to partner with Dark Slope to bring this epic series to life for Amazon Kids+, CBC, and ITV,” added Lysakowski. “It’s a unique collaboration and we’re using cutting edge technology to give kids a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to compete on a one-of-a-kind playground.”

title: NBC Celebrates 100th Anniversary With Amy Poehler, Jimmy Fallon and More Stars at Rainbow Room Soirée
description:
NBC celebrated its 100th anniversary with a star-studded party at the Rainbow Room in Manhattan.

	Amy Poehler, Jimmy Fallon, Andy Cohen, Hoda Kotb
body:
NBC celebrated its 100th anniversary with a star-studded party at the Rainbow Room in Manhattan.

	Amy Poehler, Jimmy Fallon, Andy Cohen, Hoda Kotb, Tracy Morgan, Al Roker and more celebs who work closely with the Peacock mingled in the luxury ballroom, located on the 65th floor of 30 Rock, where sushi, pasta and cocktails were served. 

	The event commemorated the very first radio broadcast of the National Broadcasting Corporation, the first such broadcast to go out across the entire United States. 
	

	Wally Feresten, aka “Cue Card Wally,” who has worked at “Saturday Night Live” since 1990 and “Late Night With Seth Meyers” since 2014, was also in attendance, writing customized cue cards for party guests.



	

					Amy Poehler, Pearlena Igbokwe and Rachel Dratch
									Nina Westervelt/NBC
	



	Top brass were also at the event, including Comcast co-CEO Mike Cavanagh and NBCUniversal execs Frances Berwick, Cesar Conde, Pearlena Igbokwe and more.

	Raising a glass to the network’s history, Cavanagh said in a toast: “NBC has played a part in shaping American culture and society for 100 years. It’s an unbelievable legacy when you think about it. We’ve gone from radio to television, black and white to color, broadcast to streaming. All these technologies have changed. How we program has changed, and how we reach consumers and audiences is completely different than it once was. But what hasn’t changed is the strength of the people who make up our company, and their courage and willingness to take big swings. And that is a defining characteristic of NBC, and why I’m so proud to be a part of it. We look forward to an incredible next century.”
	

	The cocktail party is one of many celebrations honoring NBC’s 100th anniversary. A primetime special will air live on NBC on Dec. 10, uniting legendary casts, talent and performers for musical performances, comedic tributes, and surprise reunions.

title: ‘The Body’ Creator Quinn Shephard on Quitting Acting and Turning Religious Trauma Into Queer, Catholic Ecstasy
description: At 31, Quinn Shephard is behind some of the most projects about teen girls on television. In 2024, she created Hulu’s subversive true crime series
body:
At 31, Quinn Shephard is behind some of the most projects about teen girls on television. In 2024, she created Hulu’s subversive true crime series “Under the Bridge,” and on Nov. 11, Netflix released her newest effort: “The Body,” a queer psychological drama set at a Catholic high school in 2004 that debuted at No. 3 on the streamer’s weekly viewership rankings. But 20 years ago, her foray into the teen genre began with an unauthorized adaptation of a popular book series that got trapped in development hell.
	

	“I was trying to make a movie by the time I was 10,” recalls Shephard. “My parents found offer letters that I was writing to, like, my dad’s best friend: ‘Will you play Mr. Scary in my “Junie B. Jones” adaptation?’” But the project “couldn’t get off the ground because we lost the key location,” she says, laughing. (She never remotely considered the possibility that her elementary school principal had been joking when he offered her some classrooms. “I was like, ‘OK, here’s the shooting schedule,’ and he was like, ‘No, I didn’t mean that.’ I was mad,” she says. “‘Why would you tell me I could?’ I was so fucking annoying. But I don’t think I knew how to be any other way, unfortunately.”)

	Shephard began her career, and life, as an actress. She barely remembers how it all began beyond the encouragement she received from her mother, Laurie, a former actress, and says that in her earliest memories, she’s in Prague surrounded by her family while shooting the Andie MacDowell-led drama film “Harrison’s Flowers” at just 4 years old. “I grew up in Central Jersey and went to public school, so being on set was my main access to things that felt bigger than that world,” she says. Her mother had worked in soap operas and commercials until she retired to focus on raising — and managing — Quinn. “My parents raised me to have dreams, and to believe that those dreams were possible,” Shephard says. “So when I was 15 and wrote a movie, my mom was like, ‘Let’s get into notes. How are we going to make this?’ I had a delusional confidence from growing up on set and seeing how it worked. It didn’t feel any more complicated than any other job. In fact, it felt sensible.”
	

	When asked to sum up her media diet as a kid, Shephard rattles off a list of films that includes “The Crucible,” “Girl, Interrupted,” “Jennifer’s Body,” “Donnie Darko” — you get the picture. “Stuff that’s vibey and moody with a dark sense of humor,” she says. “The Sparkle Motion sequence in ‘Donnie Darko’ was one of the moments where I was like, ‘I want to do whatever this is.’”



	

									Nick Rasmussen
	



	So she did. Through a public arts program that was “mostly just me and a bunch of boys,” Shephard began producing her own work around age 12. She and her classmates stunned their parents into silence with dark short films in which she, for example, played one of a psych ward patient’s multiple personalities. She was auditioning for professional projects at the same time, but needless to say, she wasn’t a Disney-style child actress. The audition circuit for East coast youths produced an alternative kind of star: Shephard cites Rachel Brosnahan, Taissa Farmiga and even Timothée Chalamet as some of the names running in the same circles.

	Armed with the “delusional confidence” those experiences gave her, a teenage Shephard began working on the script that would eventually become “Blame,” her debut feature film as a writer-director. “Not a single fact about how that movie got made makes any sense,” Shephard says. She ended up shooting the film at age 20 and premiering it two years later — but not before a flaky investor almost blew up the whole project in her face. “It’s something I could literally never do now. I don’t have the blind faith and stamina I had to have at that age to make that movie, and the level of ego I must have had to be like, ‘I can pull off a whole feature!’ I cannot process it, but it happened, and thank God.”

	The investor, an indie director Shephard had been working with on another project, took advantage of her moxie and naiveté to keep stringing her along — though for what reason, she still doesn’t understand. “He was always like, ‘Money’s coming. Money’s coming,’” she recalls. “I remember the last text I sent him. I was like, ‘Hey, my parents are about to putting things on credit cards. I don’t want to put us into debt. I need to know if this is real.’ And he was like, ‘Put it on the credit cards. Tell your parents it’s all good. I got you. The money’s coming.’ And he ghosted.”
	

	Shephard was already deep into the preparation process, and her high profile co-star, Chris Messina, was days away from arriving. So she and her parents decided to empty her college fund and the money she’d earned as a child actor, which had been untouched for years outside of careful investments. That got them through production, and post-production unfolded slowly: “I would do an acting job, then I would use that to pay for a sound mix. I would do another acting job, then I’d use that to get on a bus to Montreal and work with a friend of a friend’s colorist who gave me a deal.” And so on and so forth until “Blame” debuted at the Tribeca Film Festival, where it was warmly reviewed. Another one of Shephard’s co-stars, her then-girlfriend Nadia Alexander, was named best actress in a U.S. narrative feature.

	Making “Blame” led to a major transition in Shephard’s career: She quit acting. “I was so grateful for the experiences that I had as a kid, and the access that it gave me to film, but I realized that I hadn’t consciously chosen to be an actor,” she says. “I was like, ‘If I change my mind, I could always slide back in.’ But I just haven’t. It feels so foreign to me now. It’s such a distant part of myself that it’s kind of funny to me now that I used to do it.”

	She made her second film in 2022, a dramedy called “Not Okay” that taught her how difficult filmmaking is even when you step outside of the indie world. “It was actually crazy, because I was shooting a movie with Searchlight, but the process was not wildly different. You never feel like you have enough money. You never feel like you have enough time. Everything’s always hectic. It’s just that with more money, you can get cranes if you want cranes.”



	

					Left to right: “The Body” star Sofia Wylie and creator Quinn Shephard 
									Sabrina Lantos/Netflix
	



	“The Body” is Shephard’s best and most ambitious project to date, and it came from a combination of the processes behind “Blame” and Not Okay.” Like the latter, she had studio backing (this time from Netflix), but more importantly, like the former, she trusted in the merits of a script she’d written when she was younger.

	The series follows the spread of mass hysteria through a small town after a girl named Grace (Sofia Wylie) falls into a coma after attending a Halloween party where her Catholic school dance teammates pressured her to take Ecstasy. As the girls hide what they did, they pretend they’re being visited by Grace in intense religious visions. But soon enough, half the town believes that Grace is God, or at least one of his agents. They find genuine solace in worshipping her.
	

	Shephard wrote a version of the show 10 years ago without a clear thesis in mind, though she has a better idea of why the idea came to her in retrospect. “I always related to religious horror in a way that I didn’t fully understand, these themes of shame and passion and ecstasy,” she says. And as I got older and started working on this show, I was like, ‘Oh, it’s the perfect metaphor for a queer girl’s coming-of age. Worshipful experiences that give meaning to your life, and then deep repression. Religious horror has always explored that in a way that felt really accessible to me. It made sense.”



	

					Left to right: “The Body” stars Sara Boustany (Elise) and Kristina Bogic (Anya) 
									Netflix
	



	Though Shephard was never baptized into Christianity, she did occasionally going to church with her paternal grandmother — who was an Evangelical deliverance minister — as a young child. “I was so into it. I loved it. I was like, ‘I’m dancing. I’m singing. I’m talking to Jesus. I’m loving it,” she says. “But, as I’m prone to do, I took an incident a little too seriously and got very obsessed and upset.” She somehow wound up seeing a play meant for adults about “people being afraid they’re going to hell or killing themselves over adultery or something.” Shephard’s mother, who had been wracked with Catholic guilt earlier in her life and didn’t want the same for her daughter, decided that was enough was enough. But for a time, the abrupt end to her foray into Christianity only intensified Shephard’s interest: She recalls reading her children’s Bible in secret to figure out what was so forbidden about it.

	As Shephard grew up, her separation from Christianity was unsurprisingly more political (and personal) in nature. “I associated it with oppression of the queer community and rejection of people for being different,” she says. But she didn’t know how to reckon with the pull she still felt toward some sort of faith. “Like, I’ll cry if I go to a church. Especially an ecstatic, charismatic church where people are singing and dancing. It’s so moving.”

	She continues, “I’ve never been an atheist. I’ve always been curious. I’ve always believed in ghosts — I saw some when I was a kid.” But it wasn’t until working with the other writers on “The Body” that Shephard fully unpacked these experiences. “Writing this show has weirdly healed my relationship with faith to the point where I can sit with the more religious side of my family and have a really meaningful conversation about it — as long as we don’t talk about politics,” she says. “Because now I’ve had such a journey: What is my spirituality? What do I believe in? And I’ve engaged so much with journalism on unexplainable things. I’m so spiritually curious, and spent so much time talking to people about their relationship with faith for this show that I had a breakthrough, like, ‘I think I get it.’ Hopefully, it comes through that all of us who work on the show are very faith-positive, but system-critical.”
	

	There’s a throughline that runs through Shephard’s work and the films gravitated to in her youth, even beyond the obvious aesthetic elements: meditation on what it means to deeply want something, be it power, love, sex or answers. The honest beauty and painful consequences that come with desire are as alive in John Proctor and Abigail Williams in “The Crucible” as they are in the schoolgirls of “The Body.”

	As Shephard puts it, “People who go to church searching for a religious experience, and me and my friends in Silver Lake doing a guided mushroom trip and talking about connecting with ancestral energy or whatever — it’s all the same human desire.”



	

					Left to right: “The Body” stars Sarah Abbot (Olivia), Emily Roman (Claire), Kyra Pierce (Bailey), Kristina Bogic (Anya), Phallon Pierce (Brit), Michela Luci (Amy), Julia Lowe (Blair)

	This year’s International Documentary Association Documentary Awards nominations have been announced.

	Asmahan Bkerat’s “Concrete Land” leads the field with six nominations, followed by Biljana Tutorov and Petar Glomazić’s “To Hold a Mountain” with five.

	Mehrdad Oskouei and Soraya Akhlaghi’s “A Fox Under a Pink Moon” and Pegah Ahangarani’s “Rehearsals for a Revolution” also scored strong showings, earning four nominations apiece.
	

	Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s box office hit “You Can See Everything” earned three nominations, including best feature documentary, best director and best original music score, but was shut out of the cinematography and editing categories.

	IDA received a record 650 submissions from 95 countries, with 32 countries represented among this year’s nominees.

	“I couldn’t be more excited to celebrate these meaningful and creative documentaries. It’s a challenging time for documentary makers, but also a really inspiring moment for IDA and for the field,” says Ina Fichman, IDA board president. “This year we see nominees whose deeply personal stories share narratives of resistance and exile, and we see artful, innovative filmmaking that is capturing new and robust audiences.”

body:
Netflix’s sci-fi thriller “3 Body Problem” returns for Season 2 on Jan. 14.

	The series, based on the popular “Remembrance of Earth’s Past” book series by Chinese author Liu Cixin, explores complex questions about the nature of the universe, leading a group of scientists to partner with a detective to confront an existential planetary threat in the wake of the Chinese Cultural Revolution in the 1960s.


	In Season 2, “the alien invasion nears and humanity prepares to meet them — on Earth and beyond. While a space fleet embarks on a mission that spans centuries, a secret locked inside of one man’s mind might be humanity’s only hope for survival.”
	

	The trailer and teaser images give a first look at this season’s otherworldly forces as the alien invasion nears. Some are devout San-Ti followers, like Tatiana (Marlo Kelly), and will stop at nothing to help the alien agenda. 

	Returning alongside Kelly are Jovan Adepo as Saul Durand, Liam Cunningham as Thomas Wade, Eiza González as Auggie Salazar, Jess Hong as Jin Cheng, Benedict Wong as Da Shi, Sea Shimooka as Sophon and Saamer Usmani as Raj Varma. New recruits also join the human forces in Season 2, with Claudia Doumit (“SOULM8TE,” “The Boys”) joining the cast as Captain Van Rijn and Ellie de Lange (“Run Away,” “Wolf Hall,” “The Serpent”) as Ayla.

	The series is created and executive produced by David Benioff and D.B. Weiss (“Game of Thrones”) and Alexander Woo (“True Blood,” “The Terror”). The first season was released in 2024.

	See first look images and watch the trailer below.
	





	

					Jess Hong as Jin Cheng in 3 Body Problem. Cr. Netflix © 2026

									Courtesy of Netflix
	





	

					Sea Shimooka as Sophon in 3 Body Problem. Cr. Netflix © 2026

		Development/Production	

	Masterpiece PBS has announced a new period crime drama “Fleet Street” from the creators of “Miss Scarlet,” Rachael New and Ben Edwards.

	Set in 1901 London, the death of a local florist tied to the royals captures the attention of aspiring journalist Kitty Parker (Silvia Presente) and The Morning Herald reporter Samuel Wallace (Guy Remmers), giving the duo their first lead. A missing son, anonymous messages and a gruesome death send them on an investigation that could shape their careers or put them in imminent danger.

	Filming for the six-part first season will begin in December, and the series will launch in the U.K. on UKTV’s free streaming service U and air on U&Drama. “Fleet Street” is co-produced by Mikey Productions Limited and Masterpiece. Executive producing are New, Edwards, Patricia Lenahan and Patrick Irwin for Mikey Productions Limited. Susanne Simpson is the executive producer for Masterpiece, and Claire Hookway and Karin Marelle are the executive producers for UKTV. Ivan Živković serves as lead director.
	
		First Looks/Trailers	

	“My Next Guest Needs No Introduction with David Letterman” returns for its seventh season Dec. 15 on Netflix, with a new trailer available now.

	The forthcoming season of the Emmy Award-winning series features conversations with actors Matt Damon and Julia Roberts, late-night host Jimmy Kimmel and professional climber Alex Honnold. Previous guests include Barack Obama, Tina Fey, Julia Louis-Dreyfus, JAY-Z, Robert Downey Jr., Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Dave Chappelle, Michael B. Jordan, Miley Cyrus, Caitlin Clark, Billie Eilish and Adam Sandler.

	“My Next Guest Needs No Introduction with David Letterman” brings Letterman back to hosting, following his 33-year career in late night television. The series has received eight Emmy nominations in its six seasons and won for Outstanding Hosted Nonfiction Series or Special in 2024. 

	The series is produced by Jax Media/Imagine Entertainment and Worldwide Pants, Inc. Executive producers are Tom Keaney and Mary Barclay for Worldwide Pants and Justin Wilkes, Michael Steed, Isabel Richardson and Yolanda T. Cochran for Jax Media/Imagine Entertainment. Producers are Tommy Alter, John Nemeth, Hunter Speese and Adam Donnelly for Jax Media/Imagine Entertainment.
	

	Watch the trailer for “My Next Guest Needs No Introduction with David Letterman” Season 7 below.



	*

	Michael Paré (“Eddie and the Cruisers,” “Streets of Fire”) is making his vertical microseries debut in the vertTV thriller “The Squatter Hunter,” which premieres Tuesday on the vertTV app.

	Paré plays an ex-military operative hired off the books to help a grieving daughter (Chelsea Rose Cook) reclaim her childhood home from a hostile squatter (Shayne Davis) after police are unable to intervene in the civil dispute, escalating the standoff into a life-or-death showdown.

	Alongside Paré, the series stars Savoy Bailey, Diane Robin and Demetris Owens and reunites “90210” stars Tori Spelling and Brian Austin Green. It is directed by David DeCoteau from a script by Adam Rockoff.

	Watch the full trailer below:



	*

	Happy holidays from the Griffin family!

	The long-running animated sitcom “Family Guy” is celebrating with a Hulu exclusive holiday special which premieres on Nov. 30 on Hulu and Hulu on Disney+ for bundle subscribers in the U.S., and will exclusively stream internationally on Disney+ in most markets.

	The synopsis for the episode, titled “The Peter Cause,” reads: “It’s Christmas in Quahog, and Peter and the guys compete to become the town’s official Santa. Peter loses, and he can either process his disappointment in a mature manner, or give fans a memorable episode of ‘Family Guy.’ Thankfully, he chooses option number two.”

	Watch the trailer for the special below:


	
		Programming	

	Tis the season to light the Rockefeller Center Christmas Tree! The two-hour “Christmas in Rockefeller Center” special will air live on Dec. 2 at 8 p.m. ET on NBC and simulcast on Peacock.

	Cynthia Erivo will make her hosting debut and perform during the live tree lighting special. The Emmy, Tony and Grammy Award winner will be joined by Kelly Clarkson, EJAE, Kirk Franklin, Wynonna Judd, JYT, Alanis Morissette, Brad Paisley, Alex Warren and more. The Radio City Rockettes will continue their holiday performance tradition. “TODAY” anchors Carson Daly, Craig Melvin and Al Roker will also be part of the celebration.
	

	“’Christmas in Rockefeller Center’ captures the spirit and magic of the holiday season, bringing together unforgettable performances, the energy of New York and a timeless tradition that connects generations,” said Jen Neal, Executive Vice President, Live Events and Specials, NBC & Peacock. “It’s incredibly special that we get to bring this moment to life year after year and share the excitement with millions of viewers.”

	“Christmas in Rockefeller Center” is produced by Universal Television in association with Jesse Collins Entertainment. Jesse Collins, Dionne Harmon and Jeannae Rouzan-Clay executive produce, with Glenn Weiss as director.

	An additional live hour of the special will be broadcast on NBC stations and some nationwide affiliates at 7 p.m. ET. Telemundo’s simulcast of “Navidades en Rockefeller Center (Christmas in Rockefeller Center)” will air live at 9 p.m. ET. “Christmas with Snoop” will follow the special, airing at 10 p.m. ET on NBC and next day on Peacock.

	*

	Dhar Mann Studios, Fox Entertainment and Holywater Tech announced the first five original scripted vertical dramas from their multi-year partnership.

	The five series will debut on Holywater Tech’s My Drama platform, beginning Nov. 25 and rolling out weekly through Dec. 22. The series feature storylines ranging from complicated relationships and family drama to dangerous secrets and unexpected second changes. The slate was developed specifically for vertical viewing.

	“When viewers ask you to make something, you want to get it right for them. Our audience is already watching vertical dramas, and they’ve asked us to join them there,” said Erin McFarlane, Dhar Mann Studios’ head of film and TV. “We’ve taken that to heart. We want these shows to have the romance, suspense and surprises they enjoy, and to give them that connection they feel with a Dhar Mann story—seeing a little of themselves in someone and really wanting things to work out for them.”

	The 40-title slate was announced in January. It marks Dhar Mann Studios’ first major expansion into vertical dramas with Holywater Tech’s mobile-first platform, with FOX Entertainment Global’s distribution.

	The five series and their release dates are below. Subscribers can access each title a week earlier.“The Brothers Who Love Me” — Nov. 25“Rescue Mission” — Dec. 1“Married to the Wind” — Dec. 8“Rhythm of the Heart” — Dec. 15“The Rockstar Who Wants Me” — Dec. 22

									2026 Victoria's Secret
	

		
	
				

	Every James Bond is only as good as the person who’s trying to kill him.

	Throughout the franchise’s history, we’ve seen Sean Connery take on Gert Fröbe’s Goldfinger, Roger Moore tackle Christopher Walken’s Max Zorin and, in the Daniel Craig era, Mads Mikkelsen’s Le Chiffre in “Casino Royale” and Javier Bardem’s notorious Raoul Silva in “Skyfall.” In a Bond film, the movie cannot succeed without the diabolical plan and villain that’s trying to destroy the world or the shaken, not stirred man in the tux.

	After the news that Robert Pattinson has been cast to portray the infamous hero in an upcoming film from Denis Villeneuve, the search is on for the next “Bond Girl” and now the anticipated adversary that threatens his mission to keep the world safe.

	The wish list includes many familiar faces from Pattinson’s past, both in front and behind the camera and some long-shot selections that may be crazy enough to work. Whether it’s a tech messiah, a rogue spy or an heiress with a doomsday device, we’re excited. 

	Here are the 22 actors Variety would love to see go toe-to-toe with the new 007.

	Honorable mentions: Mahershala Ali, Austin Butler, Cate Blanchett, Willem Dafoe, Mia Goth, Nicholas Hoult, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Wagner Moura, Dev Patel, Matthew Rhys, Callum Turner


			
			
	Riz Ahmed
			
										
					Image Credit: Paola Kudacki for Variety				
					
				

	Riz Ahmed is skilled in dramatic roles, like his Oscar-nominated performance as a troubled drummer in “Sound of Metal.” But he’s also a master of voice and motion-capture acting, from Severus Snape in the “Harry Potter” audiobooks to the ruthless symbiote leader Riot in “Venom.” So whether he plays it straight or perhaps takes the form of a monstrous menace to Robert Pattinson’s Bond, Ahmed has the subtle, steely power to be a baddie either way.

	–Pat Saperstein

		
			
			
	Pierce Brosnan
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images for US-Ireland Alli				
					
				

	Pierce Brosnan led four James Bond films as the titular superspy in the late ’90s, so why not bring him home for one last ride as the silver-haired supervillain? 

	Brosnan, who was vocal throughout the 007 casting process, has remained a staple of the action genre 24 years after his final turn as Bond in “Die Another Day.” He recently lent his espionage expertise to Steven Soderbergh, playing the double-agent villain in his twisty spy thriller “Black Bag.” Also on the villain front, Bronsan has been stirring up trouble as the leader of the Irish mob in “Mobland,” which is wrapping its second season.

	— Jack Dunn

		
			
			
	Timothée Chalamet
			
										
					Image Credit: Chad Salvador/WWD				
					
				

	Director Denis Villeneuve is about to bring Timothée Chalamet through his villain arc in “Dune: Part Three,” and he may want to bring that tyrannical overlord energy with him to the Bond franchise. Chalamet, like Robert Pattinson, is one of Hollywood’s most in-demand stars, which makes him an intriguing on-screen rival. Chalamet has built his young career playing righteous leading men, however complicated they may be, in films like “Marty Supreme,” “A Complete Unknown” and “Wonka.” It could be time for Chalamet to stay on the dark side for a bit longer and take on cinema’s suavest spy.

	— Jack Dunn

		
			
			
	Elizabeth Debicki
			
										
					Image Credit: David Vintiner for Variety				
					
				

	If Pattinson made his case for playing Bond with Nolan’s time-bending spy thriller “Tenet,” then Debicki should also be strongly considered alongside him. The two of them had standout roles in the movie, and we’re dying for them to get some more screen time together. “He is an enigma himself,” Debicki told Variety about Pattinson’s Bond casting. “He’s beautiful, and he’s funny and he’s smart. I think he’s perfect. I’m so thrilled.”

	— Jordan Moreau

		
			
			
	Idris Elba
			
										
					Image Credit: Benedict Evans/Variety				
					
				

	Having spent so many years being tipped by the media for the 007 job — and then being asked about Bond in every interview — it feels only right that Idris Elba be given a juicy bad guy role to play. But this is no consolation prize for the Brit, who has excelled in intimidating, scene-commanding villainy on more than one occasion, including as the brooding and calculating Stringer Bell in his “The Wire” breakout, the ruthless mercenary leading a group of child soldiers in “Beasts of No Nation,” the genuine action movie baddie in “Hobbs & Shaw” and, er, the master criminal feline Macavity in “Cats.” OK, fine.

	— Alex Ritman

		
			
			
	Colin Farrell
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of ZFF/Andreas Rentz (Getty)				
					
				

	Colin Farrell has already gone toe-to-toe with Pattinson, buried under prosthetics as Oz Cobb in “The Batman.” The Oscar nominee from “The Banshees of Inisherin” has played a hit man with a conscience in films like “In Bruges” and an assassin as Bullseye in “Daredevil.” 

	Now let’s picture that Irish charm curdling into something far more dangerous, like an arms baron who’s a blast to watch even as he’s trying to kill Bond. Do it.

	— Clayton Davis

		
			
			
	Michael Fassbender
			
										
					Image Credit: Alexi Lubomirski for Variety				
					
				

	Fassbender spent years playing an empathetic villain in Fox’s “X-Men” series as a young Magneto. Now, he’s played a suave spy in last year’s surprise sleeper hit “Black Bag,” a cold assassin in David Fincher’s 2023 thriller “The Killer” and a CIA officer in “The Agency” on Paramount+. He certainly fits the bill to star in a Bond movie, perhaps as a double-crossing 00 spy who faces off against Pattinson.

	–Jordan Moreau

		
			
			
	Rebecca Ferguson
			
										
					Image Credit: Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images				
					
				

	Rebecca Ferguson has shown she can keep up with Tom Cruise’s Ethan Hunt in the “Mission: Impossible” franchise, so it could be time for her to face off against cinema’s other iconic man of mystery. 

	Outside of her three “Mission” films, she recently took on internal affairs as a high-level situation room officer in Kathryn Bigelow’s “House of Dynamite.” Ferguson is probably best known for her leading role in Apple TV’s “Silo” as Juliette Nichols, a mechanic-turned-post-apocalyptic liberator. It also helps she’s in Denis’ orbit already with the “Dune” franchise.

	She’s already a pro at unraveling a conspiracy, so she is sure to be an expert at weaving one together in the face of Bond.

	— Jack Dunn

		
			
			
	Walton Goggins
			
										
					Image Credit: Rob Latour/Variety				
					
				

	Walton Goggins is already one of Amazon’s most valuable assets, starring in Prime Video’s post-apocalyptic drama “Fallout” as a 200-year-old zombie cowboy.

	Of course, Goggins made Boyd Crowder, the silver-tongued soul of FX’s crime drama “Justified,” one of his most memorable creations. Plus, he nearly stole the show on HBO’s anthology series “The White Lotus” as the haunted Rick.

	Some of the best Bond villains are a little unhinged and completely charming, and Goggins brings both.

	–Clayton Davis

		
			
			
	Jake Gyllenhaal
			
										
					Image Credit: Billy Kidd/Variety				
					
				

	Villeneuve and Gyllenhaal have already worked together on “Prisoners” back in 2013, and they’re long overdue for a reunion. Gyllenhaal has played a wide variety of unsettling bad guys in recent years, like a grimy journalist in “Nightcrawler,” a theatrical Mysterio in “Spider-Man” and a smooth-talking criminal in “Ambulance.” He’s also bulked up and trained in UFC fighting for two “Road House” movies. His Bond villain could mix all of these past roles into one and be a true chameleon.

	— Jordan Moreau

		
			
			
	Tom Hiddleston
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty				
					
				

	Isn’t it safe to say that AMC’s “The Night Manager” was pretty much Tom Hiddleston’s 007 audition tape?

	He reprised his role as former British intelligence operative Jonathan Pine earlier this year in the second season streaming on Prime Video. However, the tuxedo never came, so maybe being another scene-stealing bad boy can get him into the fold. As Loki in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, Hiddleston proved audiences will adore a villain even while he betrays everyone. 

	Maybe casting him as a disgraced MI6 golden boy, or an agent who was supposed to get the number but then didn’t, will let him spend the whole movie proving he actually deserved it.

	— Clayton Davis

		
			
			
	Angelina Jolie
			
										
					Image Credit: Michael Buckner/Variety				
					
				

	Angelina Jolie has already shared the screen with one 007 when Daniel Craig played her rival in “Lara Croft: Tomb Raider” (2001). What if she took a shot at the next one?

	The Oscar winner of “Girl, Interrupted” has played both sides of the spy game in films like “Salt” and “Mr. & Mrs. Smith.” She also gave Disney one of its most iconic villains in the live-action format with “Maleficent.” 

	Let her bring a menacing rage to the MI6 team and watch what happens.

	–Clayton Davis

		
			
			
	Daniel Kaluuya
			
										
					Image Credit: Variety via Getty Images				
					
				

	Daniel Kaluuya is reuniting with his “Judas and the Black Messiah” director, Shaka King, on a new Amazon MGM movie, “The Parlay,” so technically he’s already in the family, right?

	For anyone who saw Steve McQueen’s “Widows,” they’ll remember how terrifying the Oscar winner can be as he played the enforcer Jatemme and delivered one of the most chilling henchmen of the past decade. Let’s not forget “Black Panther,” where he played W’Kabi, the trusted friend who betrays his king.

	Once thrown out as a worthy contender to play Bond, this Londoner, with his knack for exuding menace, would have MI6 very worried.

	— Clayton Davis

		
			
			
	Barry Keoghan
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	Barry Keoghan has already said that, rather than Bond, he’d prefer to play the villain. Still, he’s certainly got the credentials to prove it. From a sinister teen who embarks on a campaign of revenge in “The Killing of a Sacred Deer” to a swaggering, volatile gangster in “Calm with Horses” to the murderous manipulator of “Saltburn,” the Irishman has shown he could be 007’s perfect, cherubic master of menace. And then there’s that deleted scene in “The Batman” as the Joker opposite Pattinson. Time for a proper face-off between the two.

	— Alex Ritman

		
			
			
	Cillian Murphy
			
										
					Image Credit: dpa/picture alliance via Getty I				
					
				

	From Nolan to Villeneuve, Murphy could follow Robert Pattinson from one major director to another. Murphy hit the lotto with his “Oppenheimer” Oscar win, and playing a Bond villain could be his second wave. We know he’s up to the challenge after seeing him as J. Robert Oppenheimer, the Scarecrow in “Batman Begins” and Tommy Shelby in “Peaky Blinders.” Aside from a cameo in “28 Years Later: The Bone Temple,” Netflix’s “Peaky Blinders” movie and a return in “A Quiet Place 3,” Murphy’s slate has been too quiet since “Oppenheimer” and a Bond movie would be the perfect big-screen welcome back.

	— Jordan Moreau

		
			
			
	Brad Pitt
			
										
					Image Credit: Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images				
					
				

	Upon learning that Pattinson would be Bond, Pitt pitched himself to play the villain at his “Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” premiere. Pitt has produced “Mickey 17” and “The Lost City of Z,” both of which starred Pattinson, so the two already have a connection. “I love what he’s been doing. I love his choices. I think he’s the real deal. That’s good. A good call, I like it,” Pitt said, then threw his hat in the ring to play the bad guy. “I’d like to do that. My man Javier [Bardem] did it so well. It’s tall shoes, but I’d take that on.”

	–Jordan Moreau

		
			
			
	Jesse Plemons
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	Nobody in Hollywood makes politeness more terrifying than Jesse Plemons.

	He was Todd, the soft-spoken killer of AMC’s crime series “Breaking Bad.” In Alex Garland’s “Civil War,” he turned one question, “What kind of American are you?“ into one of the frightening scenes of the year, in a one-scene wonder, no less.

	A Bond villain who never raises his voice and never apologizes before he pulls the trigger. That’s what exactly Plemons does best.

	The Oscar nominee of “The Power of the Dog,” who won Best Actor at Cannes for “Kinds of Kindness,” is playing Plutarch Heavensbee in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” this year, a role originated by the late Philip Seymour Hoffman. And famously, also played a villain in “Mission: Impossible III” (2006).

	Let’s continue the trajectory.

	— Clayton Davis

		
			
			
	Florence Pugh
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	Florence Pugh may be on many fans’ lists as a potential Bond girl (and so did Variety), but it seems the Brit — who stars alongside Robert Pattinson in “Dune: Part Three” — would rather go a different route. Speaking at Elle’s Women in Hollywood event shortly after 007 was cast, she said she’d messaged Villeneuve to say: “Congratulations on finding your Bond, nice catch. Any villains the size of a 5ft 4in female?” While Pugh’s roles haven’t yet seen her dip into full-scale global terrorism, as Cathy in the recent “East of Eden” adaptation, she has shown she could certainly explore her darker side.

	— Alex Ritman

		
			
			
	Bill Skarsgård
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	With his shape-shifting ability to transform into a menacing clown or a cadaverous vampire, Bill Skarsgård can become just about any villain the Bond creative team imagines. 

	Skarsgård’s roles in “It,” “Nosferatu,” “Barbarian,” and “The Crow” are just a few of the horror-tinged roles he’s inhabited, suggesting his take on a Bond villain could lean more toward the grotesquely menacing side. The Swedish actor even appeared with Robert Pattinson, a fellow famous vampire, in the Netflix movie “The Devil All the Time,” though they didn’t share any scenes. 

	–Pat Saperstein

		
			
			
	Kristen Stewart
			
										
					Image Credit: Variety				
					
				

	As soon as Pattinson’s name was floated as 007, hordes of Twihards were immediately fan-casting Stewart to give the Bond universe a “Twilight” crossover. But instead of playing a Bond Girl, Stewart would be a much more entertaining choice as a villain. Please, Amazon MGM, make this ultimate Bella Swan and Edward Cullen fan fiction come true. Better yet, cast Taylor Lautner as a henchman to Stewart’s Bond villain.

	— Jordan Moreau

		
			
			
	Tilda Swinton
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	A great James Bond villain is known for their striking, singular presence – and who better to provide that presence than Tilda Swinton? Her otherworldly, androgynous persona has been put to good use by everyone from the Avengers to Wes Anderson, Bong Joon Ho and the Coen brothers, and she could easily switch on the evil vibes as a Bond villain. Swinton hasn’t worked with Robert Pattinson yet, but Pattinson is a big admirer of her performance in 2008’s “Julia.” “I think that’s one of the great performances, and it’s kind of criminally underseen,” he told Rotten Tomatoes.

	–Pat Saperstein

		
			
			
	Fernanda Torres
			
										
					Image Credit: Getty Images				
					
				

	In “I’m Still Here,” Fernanda Torres played Eunice Paiva, a woman standing up to a military dictatorship and the role earned her a Golden Globe statue and an Oscar nomination for best actress. While on the awards circuit, the Brazilian star knew exactly what she wanted to do with her next big venture: play a Bond villain.

	“I would love to be the secretary of a James Bond villain,” she said on the Variety Awards Circuit Podcast. “And just say, ‘He will be waiting for you in the next room, Mr. Bond.’ That’s it. That’s my dream. Just this line. That’s all I want to do.”

	Imagine Torres as the power behind the throne: a Rio de Janeiro media baroness who smiles for the cameras while quietly buying off half the government? 

	Give her what she wants!

	— Clayton Davis

		
	
	


	
		More from Variety

schema.headline: The Next Bond Villain: From Idris Elba to Kristen Stewart, 22 Actors Who Should Face Off Against Robert Pattinson

            Rob Kardashian wanted to do something nice for a loyal family member ... so he contacted some people he knows and got her vintage vehicle fully torqued ... and it's all on video.
      
    
            Here's the deal ... Cici Bussey is Robert Kardashian Sr.'s cousin who has stayed close with Rob, his sisters, and Kris Jenner.

            The team got to work ... and you've gotta watch the clip to see the incredible results ... including the convertible top, new interior, paint touch-up, rechromed bumpers, upgraded stereo, and new tires.
      
    
            We're told the team kept everything time-period correct ... restoring it to the OG factory look.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            Cici -- who used to drive the car with her husband before his recent passing -- was clearly emotional when she saw the car ... and Rob told her in a FaceTime call he's just glad she's happy.
      
    
            On "Fully Torqued: Unleashed" with Steve Pazmany, which features the host fixing up sick cars, which premieres November 20 on Prime. Other guests include DeAndre Hopkins, Gordon Ryan, and Brendan Schaub.

            New details are emerging about the death of Heidi Gardner's boyfriend, Ray Tintori ... including exactly where the filmmaker was found inside his New York City apartment.
      
    
            Law enforcement sources tell TMZ ... a friend of Heidi's requested a wellness check, and when authorities entered Ray's apartment, they discovered him dead on the kitchen floor ... sitting with his back against the refrigerator.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            As we previously reported, the FDNY received a call requesting a wellness check at 8:43 AM on November 10 ... sending fire and EMS personnel to Ray's apartment on East 5th Street in Manhattan's East Village.
      

            EMS pronounced Ray dead at the scene, and the case was subsequently turned over to the NYPD.
      
    
            We're told Ray's death appears to be from natural causes ... though the medical examiner is conducting an autopsy to determine his exact cause of death.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported, no drugs were found at the scene.
      
    
            We broke the news Monday that Ray had died at 43 ... with the New York City Office of Chief Medical Examiner telling us his death was under investigation.
      
    
            Sources with direct knowledge told us Heidi was grieving the loss and surrounded by family and friends during the difficult time.
      
    
            Ray was a filmmaker known for directing short films and music videos ... and was part of the filmmaking collective behind the Oscar-nominated movie "Beasts of the Southern Wild."
